Convert a published LD reference panel onto your SNP set

convertLDref.Rd

Reads an LD reference panel distributed by another method and converts it, one chromosome at a time, onto the SNPs and allele coding of your analysis. Currently format = "prscs": the PRS-CS / PRS-CSx panels (for example ldblk_ukbb_afr), one HDF5 file per chromosome (ldblk_<panel>_chr<c>.hdf5, groups blk_<k> with ldblk and snplist) and the panel's SNP table (snpinfo_<panel>_hm3, columns CHR SNP BP A1 A2 MAF).

Usage

convertLDref(dir, SNP.info, format = c("prscs"))

Arguments

dir

The panel directory (holding the .hdf5 files and the snpinfo_* table).

SNP.info

A data.frame of your SNPs on ONE chromosome, in your order: SNP (rsID), CHR, REF, ALT.

format

The panel's format. Only "prscs" for now.

Value

A list: XtX (a dgCMatrix over the SNPs found, dimnames the rsIDs, in the order of SNP.info), keep (the rows of SNP.info it covers), missing (the rows it does not, with the reason), blocks (the number of panel blocks used) and sign.flipped (how many SNPs had their sign flipped).

Details

The panel's own LD blocks are kept: PRS-CS stores only the LD within each block, so the result is block LD on PRS-CS's partition and cannot be converted to chromosome LD or to other blocks (see convertLD). Signs are aligned to the ALT allele of SNP.info: an entry r_ij is multiplied by s_i s_j, with s = +1 where the panel's A1 is your ALT and -1 where it is your REF. A SNP of SNP.info that the panel lacks, or whose alleles differ, is not filled in: it is reported in missing, and the LD covers the rest. Nothing is shrunk.

Requires the Bioconductor package rhdf5.

See also

convertLD, calLD, BRIERs

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ld1 = convertLDref("ldblk_ukbb_afr", SNP.info = snps[snps$CHR == 1, ])
snps1 = snps[snps$CHR == 1, ][ld1$keep, ]
} # }
